overview.getStarted: Start by registering the environmental aspects of your main activities. The assistant can suggest aspects for an activity.
overview.requirementsIntro: The laws and other requirements that apply, the environmental objectives and how well ISO 14001 is documented.
overview.noObligations: No environmental obligations are registered yet.
overview.coverageCounts: {{ covered }} of {{ applicable }} requirements are documented

aspects.title: Aspects and impacts
aspects.subtitle: How your activities, products and services interact with the environment, and which of them are significant.
aspects.processFilter: Showing the aspects of one process.

notices.controls: This aspect is significant, but nothing controls it yet. Link a procedure, process or objective, or describe the controls.
notices.plan: This aspect can occur in an abnormal situation or an emergency, but no active emergency plan covers it.
notices.review: The review was due {{ date }}. Check that the aspect is still correct.
notices.unscored: The aspect has not been scored yet, so you cannot tell whether it is significant.

aspect.processHint: Pick the process the activity belongs to, if it is in Processes. The activity text is kept.
aspect.suggestHint: Describe the activity above and let the assistant suggest its usual aspects. Check each suggestion before you use it.
aspect.noSuggestions: No suggestions came back. Try describing the activity in more detail.
aspect.suggestionApplied: The suggestion is filled in as a draft. Check it and add the scores.
aspect.stagesHint: "After use" is reuse and recycling; "Waste treatment and landfill" is what happens to what cannot be reused.

methodSummary.sum: Score each criterion from {{ min }} to {{ max }}. The weighted scores are added up; {{ threshold }} or more is significant.
methodSummary.product: Score each criterion from {{ min }} to {{ max }}. The scores are multiplied; {{ threshold }} or more is significant.

aspect.scoreLine: Score {{ score }} of {{ max }} · significant from {{ threshold }}
aspect.scoreIncomplete: Score every criterion to assess the aspect.
aspect.overrideNotice: Significance was set by hand. The method gives: {{ computed }}. Reason: {{ reason }}
aspect.obligationsHint: ISO 14001 6.1.3: which laws, permits and other requirements apply to this aspect.
aspect.obligationsFormHint: Pick the laws, permits and other requirements that apply. They are shown on the aspect, and the obligation lists the aspect too.
aspect.noObligations: No obligations are linked. Add them when you edit the aspect.
aspect.obligationsNoAccess: You cannot read Laws and regulations, so obligations cannot be linked here.
aspect.controlsHint: ISO 14001 8.1: how the aspect is kept under control, in writing and as linked procedures, processes, objectives and risks.
aspect.controlsFormHint: Describe the controls here. After saving, link procedures, processes and objectives from the aspect's page.
aspect.noControlsSignificant: This aspect is significant, but no operational controls are described or linked yet.
aspect.plansHint: ISO 14001 8.2: the emergency plans that cover this situation.
aspect.noPlan: No emergency plan covers this aspect.
aspect.deleteMessage: {{ code }} is removed from the register and its open tasks are cancelled. The history is kept.

plans.title: Emergency plans
plans.subtitle: How you prepare for and respond to emergencies that could harm people or the environment, and the drills that test it.

notices.drill: The plan has not been tested in the last year. Hold a drill or a tabletop exercise.
notices.revision: Open tasks to revise the plan after a drill: {{ count }}
notices.noAspects: The plan is not linked to the aspects it covers.

plan.aspectsHint: The abnormal and emergency situations from the aspects register that this plan prepares for.
plan.aspectsFormHint: Pick the aspects whose abnormal or emergency situations this plan handles. Those aspects then show that they have a plan.
plan.draftNeedsScenario: Describe the scenario first, so the assistant knows what to plan for.
plan.draftTitle: Suggested response (check and adapt it before use)
plan.contactsHint: Who to contact in an emergency. Pick people in the organisation, or add external contacts such as the fire service or a supplier.
plan.drillRhythmHint: How often the plan is tested. The owner gets a task when the next drill is due.
plan.scheduleDrills: Remind the owner to hold drills on a fixed rhythm
plan.firstDrillHint: When the first drill is due. Leave it empty to start from today.
plan.noProcedure: No response has been written yet.
plan.deleteMessage: {{ code }} is removed and its drill reminders stop. Drills and history are kept.

drill.none: No drills recorded yet. Test the plan with a drill or a tabletop exercise.
drill.participantsHint: Pick the people in the organisation who took part. Their participation is kept as evidence.
drill.revisionHint: The plan owner gets a task to revise the plan, due in 30 days.
drill.realEventHint: After saving, you can record the event as a deviation so the cause is followed up.
drill.deviationPromptTitle: Record the event as a deviation?
drill.deviationPromptMessage: A real event should be followed up as a deviation, so the cause is found and fixed. The deviation is linked to this event.
drill.deleteMessage: The drill is removed from the plan's drill history.

metrics.title: Measuring and monitoring
metrics.subtitle: Energy, water, waste, emissions and materials measured over time, so you can see the trend and whether you meet your targets.

metric.unitHint: For example kWh, m3, kg, l or tonnes.
metric.targetFormHint: A target and a baseline let you judge the numbers against criteria (ISO 14001 9.1.1). The target is for a whole year.
metric.noTarget: No target is set. Set one to see whether the trend goes the right way.

targetText.decrease: At most {{ value }} {{ unit }} a year by {{ year }}
targetText.increase: At least {{ value }} {{ unit }} a year by {{ year }}

metric.noObjectives: Not linked to an environmental objective or KPI yet.
metric.emissionsHint: Fill this in if the indicator causes greenhouse gas emissions. The emissions page then counts it.
metric.scheduleCollection: Remind the owner to record a value on a fixed schedule
metric.trendEmpty: No measurements in this period yet.
metric.axisUnit: Values in {{ unit }}. The dashed line is the target per period.
metric.retiredNotice: This indicator is retired. Its measurements are kept, but new ones cannot be recorded.
metric.deleteMessage: {{ code }} and its reminders are removed. The history is kept.

measurement.title: Record a measurement
measurement.evidenceHint: Attach the invoice, meter photo or report the value comes from.
measurement.evidenceAfterSave: After saving you can attach the invoice or meter photo as evidence.
measurement.deleteMessage: The value is removed from the trend and the emission figures.

emissions.title: Greenhouse gas emissions
emissions.subtitle: Emissions per emission category (scope) and per indicator, calculated from your measurements and emission factors.
emissions.notMeasuredHint: No indicator with an emission factor is in this category yet. That is not the same as zero.
emissions.gapsHint: These indicators have data, but are left out because something is missing.
emissions.noDataTitle: No emissions recorded for this year
emissions.noData: Add an emission factor and an emission category to the indicators that cause emissions, and record values.
emissions.exportFailed: The report could not be downloaded. Try again in a moment.

scoring.title: Assessment method
scoring.subtitle: How aspects are scored and when an aspect counts as significant. One method applies to the whole organisation.
scoring.defaultNotice: You are using the default method. Adapt it to your organisation and save.
scoring.maxScore: The highest possible total is {{ max }}.
scoring.criteriaHint: Describe each criterion and what each score means. Assessors see the descriptions when they score, so everyone scores the same way.
scoring.levelsTitle: What each score means ({{ min }}–{{ max }})
scoring.levelsHint: One short line per score, in Norwegian and English.
scoring.legalRule: An aspect with a linked legal or other requirement is always significant
scoring.emergencyRule: An aspect that can occur in an emergency is always significant
scoring.confirmMessage: When you save, every aspect is scored again with the new method. Changes in score or significance are recorded in each aspect's history.
scoring.noHistory: The method has not been changed yet.

errors.scaleMin: Use a whole number from 0 to 99.
errors.scaleMax: Use a whole number from 1 to 100.

errors.weight: Use a weight above 0 and up to 10.
errors.server: This value was not accepted. Check it and try again.

review.title: Mark as reviewed
review.message: Confirm that the information is still correct, and set the date of the next review.

fields.outcome: How well did the response work?
fields.name: Name

reasons.score: The score is at or above the threshold

ask.label: Ask about this
ask.scoring: How should I score this aspect against our significance criteria? Explain each criterion with an example.
ask.aspectField: What counts as an environmental aspect for this activity, and how do I tell it apart from the impact?
ask.controlsField: Which operational controls would keep this aspect under control? Suggest procedures, checks and who should be responsible.
ask.summariseAspect: Summarise this environmental aspect: the impact, why it is or is not significant, which obligations apply and whether the controls are good enough.
ask.explainSignificance: Explain why this aspect is or is not significant under our method, and what would change the result.
ask.summarisePlan: Summarise this emergency plan and tell me what is missing for good preparedness under ISO 14001 8.2.
ask.procedure: Is this response clear enough for someone under pressure? Suggest improvements.
ask.procedureField: Help me write the response for this scenario as short, numbered steps.
ask.drillLessons: What do the drills recorded for this plan tell us, and what should we improve in the plan?
ask.explainTrend: Explain the trend of this indicator against its target, and suggest what may be behind it.
ask.methodField: How should we measure this indicator reliably, and what should we write down about the method?
ask.targetField: What would be a realistic yearly target for this indicator, and how do I set a baseline?
ask.emissionFactor: Which emission factor (kg CO₂e per {{ unit }}) should I use for this indicator, and where do I find a reliable source?
ask.scoringMethod: How should we set up the method for assessing the significance of environmental aspects? Suggest criteria, a scale and a threshold.
